title: Transverse vs longitudinal
examples: What is the difference between a wave on a rope and sound?
Can you show me a picture of a transverse wave?
How does sound travel through different materials?

explain.say: Today we are learning about two types of waves. We will look at transverse and longitudinal waves. These waves move energy through a medium. A medium is anything that can vibrate, like air or water.

A transverse wave moves up and down or side to side. The wave moves perpendicular to the direction of energy travel. Think about a wave moving across a taut rope. The parts move up and down as the wave passes.

items: Label: Medium vibrates up and down

explain.say: A longitudinal wave moves in parallel to the direction of energy travel. These waves involve pushing and pulling the medium. Sound waves are a very common example of this type of wave. They create areas of high and low density.

items: Label: Medium vibrates back and forth

explain.say: In a longitudinal wave, we see compressions and rarefactions. Compression is where the particles are packed closely together. Rarefaction is the area where the particles are spread apart.
When you hear a shout, the sound waves are longitudinal. The air particles compress and then rarefy as the sound moves to your ear. This shows the wave moving parallel to the sound direction.
A real-life example is shaking a garden hose. If you shake it side to side, you make a transverse wave. If you push and pull the hose along the ground, you create a longitudinal wave.

faq.q: What is the main difference between the two wave types?
faq.a: Transverse waves shake up and down, while longitudinal waves push and pull back and forth. You can also see this by looking at the direction of particle movement.
asks: How do I tell them apart?
Does the wave move across or along?

faq.a: Yes, sound waves in air or solids are generally longitudinal. They cause compressions and rarefactions as they travel through the medium.
asks: What kind of wave is sound?

faq.q: What causes the compressions and rarefactions?
faq.a: They are caused by the vibrations of the particles in the medium. When particles bunch up, that is a compression zone.
asks: What is happening with the air molecules?
Why do we get these spots?

faq.q: Does the wave itself move, or does the medium move?
faq.a: Only the energy moves through the medium, not the actual particles themselves. The particles just vibrate back and forth or up and down.
asks: Do the air particles travel with the sound?

faq.q: Can I see a transverse wave in everyday life?
faq.a: Yes, ripples on a pond are a good example of a transverse wave. The water moves up and down, but the wave travels across the surface.
asks: Where can I see transverse waves?

facts: Transverse waves shake perpendicular to travel.
Longitudinal waves shake parallel to travel.
Sound waves are an example of longitudinal waves.
Compression means particles are close together.

quiz.say: A wave moving across a rope is best described as:
quiz.show: Rope wave motion: Up and down
quiz.why: The rope moves up and down, which is perpendicular to the direction the wave travels.

wrong.0: This is wrong because longitudinal waves involve pushing and pulling, not up and down shaking.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the motion is orderly, not random.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the motion is strictly up and down, not in a circle.

quiz.say: Sound waves in air create areas of:
quiz.why: Sound waves are longitudinal, meaning they create areas where particles are squeezed together and areas where they are spread out.

wrong.0: This describes transverse waves, not the density changes in sound.
wrong.1: Sound travels in relatively straight lines in uniform air.
wrong.2: While speed can change, the characteristic pattern is compression and rarefaction.

quiz.say: If a wave moves along the ground like sound, what is its motion relative to travel?
quiz.why: Since sound travels by pushing and pulling, its particle motion is parallel to the direction the energy moves.

wrong.1: Perpendicular motion describes transverse waves like ripples on water.
wrong.2: The particles do not move in a circle when sound passes.
wrong.3: The wave pattern is systematic, not random.
